window_scheme.excluded: OLS, which diverges and would dominate any average

max_predictability.tuned_on: a 75/25 split inside the training window; the test period was scored once

entropy.note: 1.0 permutation entropy means no ordinal structure at all

latent_state.reading: the smoothed figure is what a perfectly informed observer of the common driver could explain; the forecast figure is what is available in advance. The gap is the size of the prize for observing the hidden state, and the remainder above the smoothed figure is irreducible

band_notes.Consumption-shaped: One or two Store purchases; the size a player buying premium would post
band_notes.Heavy consumption: Several purchases at once, or a season of premium bought ahead
band_notes.Above the fee cap: Large enough that the 1,000,000 GP fee cap binds (1,350 TC), which is where arbitrage and speculation become cost-efficient
band_notes.Wholesale: Tens of thousands of coins; consistent with converting money to gold at scale, or with an inventory position

profiles.stimulus: GP received per unit of money
profiles.prediction: Sells more coins when the GP price is high, which caps rallies
profiles.evidence: Sell-side depth is only 16% of resting coins, so this side is thin and its withdrawal would move the price

profiles.prediction: Buys in Store-sized lots, insensitive to price, on a monthly cycle
profiles.evidence: 64% of offers are under 500 TC but only 1.6% of coins

profiles.prediction: Buys on momentum; would show as return autocorrelation
profiles.evidence: Momentum carries no out-of-sample value (Section 6.6.2), so this motive leaves no detectable footprint in prices

profiles.prediction: Trades only when the gap clears the fee
profiles.evidence: The band sits at 1.79%; the average trade nets below zero while the strongest decile held a month does not (Sections 6.6.10, 7.7)

profiles.profile: Farmer, gold to coin to money
profiles.stimulus: Farm hours against the coin price and the outside money price
profiles.prediction: Buys coins to export value; would show as coins leaving the game
profiles.evidence: 5,579,274 TIB outstanding is coins held outside the in-game system (Section 5.8)

profiles.prediction: Never touches the coin market; is pure gold supply
profiles.evidence: Invisible in this data by construction, and a standing limitation

participants.caveat: the mapping from order size to motive is a hypothesis; what is measured is the size distribution and the imbalance within each band

sample.quality_filter: coverage >= 80%, non-partial date, converged price worlds

specification.claim_scope: descriptive temporal association and out-of-sample prediction; not causal

group_specific_models.target: Seven-day change in a world's log-price deviation from the cross-world mean
hierarchy: PvP, regions and BattlEye cohorts pooled

launch_phase_models.definition: Regular worlds created inside the sample, from age 0 through 540 days
launch_phase_models.target: Seven-day change in a launch world's log-price deviation from the mature converged-world mean
launch_phase_models.battleye_not_split: Launch cohorts are overwhelmingly green; BattlEye separation is not identified

regime_splits.regime: index at or near a high

long_horizon_production.emission_note: kill counts span the full joint sample; the monetary emission series still covers only 2025-12-05 onward, because reconstructing GP needs per-creature detail that lives only in the raw archive
long_horizon_production.monetary_not_estimable_note: the emission series spans 0.65 years, so horizons of 365 days leave fewer than 3 independent windows in 18 of 18 cells; those cells are reported as not estimable rather than as findings

families.correction: Sidak over the lag grid, then Benjamini-Hochberg across series
families.why: the smallest p across six lags is not a p-value, so two searches are paid for

families.family: Model comparison against a random walk
families.correction: Benjamini-Hochberg at 5% across every model-horizon cell
families.why: one family: every model tried on every horizon and target

families.correction: Benjamini-Hochberg, then a per-date re-test of every survivor
families.why: four families of specification searched jointly over horizons and windows
0.65 years of emission cannot support horizons to a year; untested rather than rejected

families.correction: per-date Newey-West and a calendar-span window count
families.why: strength by holding period and signal decile, tested as one grid
reported as magnitudes; the conclusion rests on the size and sign, not on any cell clearing a threshold

families.correction: joint chi-squared rather than per-coefficient tests
families.why: eleven month dummies asked as one question, which is what a joint test is for
descriptive contrasts between subsamples, not a search for a significant one

families.correction: surrogate distribution rather than an analytic p-value
families.why: the null is generated, so the comparison is to a simulated distribution

testing_ledger.principle: a family is a set of tests asked as one question; correcting across families that answer different questions would be as wrong as not correcting within one
